claim: An azimuth byte does not scale an angle and does not have 128 values. Two is added to it, the result is shifted right two places, the centre is taken off, and what is left is stopped at 15 either way -- so the byte reaches 31 positions 12 degrees apart, from L180 through 0 to R180. The added two is the rounding of a divide by four and nothing else: without it every position would sit a byte off the one the page prints. Twenty nine of the positions are 4 byte values wide and the two poles are 6, which is not a widening of those positions but the clamp taking the two values at each end of the byte the shift would have carried past them. The two poles are one place: half a turn to the left is half a turn to the right, and the page writes that into both cells rather than leaving it to be noticed.
why_not_named: There is nothing to call it. A shift, a rounding term and a clamp are three lines of whatever the part is written in, and naming them would be naming arithmetic.

measurements.read_as: The byte at all 128 of its settings on the type that does nothing else, read between the two outputs rather than in one of them. Every one of the byte's 127 steps is a place the rule says the reading either moves or stands still, and nothing in the rule was fitted to anything measured, so the sweep had 127 chances to contradict it.

The same takes read per band. It is what says the placement is a filtering of each channel rather than a gain on it: the flattest setting already spreads 2.86 decibels over the bands and the widest spreads 23.38, so the broadband figure above is an average over a separation that is not one number. A gain moved between two outputs would spread the same amount at every setting.

01 71 in Speaker, at one setting inside each of the thirty-one positions. Not another test of the rule -- a grid that lands one setting in each position samples a table and a law at the same places -- but a reading of what else is true of the byte.

01 70 in Phones, at one setting inside each of the thirty-one positions, taken ten seconds after each write instead of at once. Not another test of the rule -- a grid that lands one setting in each position samples a table and a law at the same places -- but the first reading of this type that is of a placement rather than of the movement towards one. Three takes at each setting and all three kept, so a setting the ten seconds did not reach says so in its own numbers rather than in a note.

values: Every setting of the sweep beside this whose takes spread by more than 0.05 dB, which is the coarsest its settled settings spread by and the same figure the band reading keeps a band by. The rule reads the takes' disagreement with each other, not the reading's disagreement with anything, so which settings are here does not depend on what the answer turned out to be. Read over every take rather than over the last two: a setting whose last two agree can still have a first take the band reading throws the whole setting away for, and eleven of them did.
measurements.read_as: The settings of 01 70 in Phones whose own takes said ten seconds had not been enough, asked again after thirty. Which settings those are is a rule applied to the takes' disagreement with each other and not to the reading's disagreement with anything, so what was re-asked could not depend on what the answer would be. The rule is the spread over every take and not the gap between the last two: written the second way it called eleven settings settled whose first take the band reading throws the whole setting away for, and the run was made again over the settings the corrected rule names.

document_rows.read_as: The whole column is the data and every one of its settings is a place the rule can be wrong. A rule with a free number per position would fit it and mean nothing; this one has no free number at all -- the centre, the step and the stop are each read off the page's own labels, not fitted -- so it had 128 chances to miss and missed none.
Which addresses the column belongs to. Both are the first parameter of a three-dimensional placement type, and no other row of the list refers to this column.

era_priors.prior: A placement of this period is stored as an index into a short table of positions, not as an angle, and the index is got out of the byte with a shift rather than a divide.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: Positions that are not evenly spaced in the byte, or a count of them that is not one more than twice a power of two minus one -- either would say the byte is being divided rather than shifted.

adds: The page states a setting at each of the byte's values and says nothing about how one becomes the other. What is added is that it is a shift and not a divide, that the rounding term is two, that the ends are a clamp rather than two wider positions, and that the whole column is 31 positions and not 128. A reader rendering this parameter needs the rule; a reader checking it needs to know which part of the shape was fitted, and none of it was.
what_it_would_change: Anything rendering these two types has to put the sound somewhere, and the byte it is handed reaches thirty-one places rather than a continuum. Round it the other way and every position sits one byte off; leave the clamp out and the two byte values at each end of the range land past the pole.

a_pair_that_is_one_setting.what: The two ends of this byte are the same place, which is why a screen asking a parameter at the two ends of what its address accepts asks this one twice where it is. One such null was published conclusive before the column was read.
a_pair_that_is_one_setting.why_it_is_not_evidence_for_this_claim: It is evidence that two byte values sound alike, which is the weakest thing the rule says and the one thing a run at the ends could have found. It is named here so that a reader does not take it for a test of the rule.

refuted_by: A reading of either slot that puts the output somewhere else at any setting: a change between two byte values this rule puts on one position, or no change between two it puts on neighbouring ones, judged against what the same pair of takes says a position differs from itself by. One position out of thirty-one landing elsewhere refutes it, because nothing in it was fitted to be moved.
could_have_been_refuted_by: A sweep of the azimuth byte reading the two outputs against each other at the byte values either side of each of the thirty boundaries this rule puts in, and inside each of the thirty-one runs it puts between them. The rule is wrong if the reading moves inside a position or stands still across one. That run has now been made at every setting of the byte: 30 of 30 boundaries moved, and of 97 neighbouring pairs the rule puts on one position, 5 moved at all and none of them by as much as a tenth of the smallest boundary.

alternatives.reading: The unit does not hold the table its manual prints. What is claimed here is a reading of a page, and a page is the publisher's account rather than the part's.
alternatives.why_it_stands: Nothing has been measured on this byte except a pair at its two ends, which this rule and every alternative to it call one place. The page cannot settle it and no reading has been taken.

separated_by.observable: Where the sound sits between the two outputs, at the byte values either side of each boundary.

predicts.a-byte-rounded-to-a-quarter-and-clamped: 31 positions, moving at 30 boundaries and nowhere else

separated_by.what_the_run_was: `balance` over the whole byte, 128 settings, two takes each and four at two of them. The stage reads both outputs, which is why it exists; the sentence this alternative carried before -- that no run here could be made -- named a limit of one stage as a limit of the archive.

alternatives.refuted_by: The sweep. The part holds the table's shape exactly: 31 runs of byte values, 4 wide except the two at the ends which are 6, with every boundary where the rule puts it and none anywhere else. That is not a page's account being repeated, it is a hundred and twenty-seven predictions coming back right.
alternatives.what_it_does_not_settle: What the page prints beside each of those positions. The shape is the part's and the degrees are still the publisher's, which is the alternative below rather than this one.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The sweep. The part holds the table's shape exactly: 31 runs of byte values, 4 wide except the two at the ends which are 6, with every boundary where the rule puts it and none anywhere else. That is not a page's account being repeated, it is a hundred and twenty-seven predictions coming back right.

alternatives.reading: The column is a table of 31 entries the byte's top bits index, written out rather than computed.
alternatives.why_it_is_equivalent: A shift with a rounding term and a table holding what the shift returns give the same position at every one of the byte's values, so no reading of the output can tell them apart -- which is the same shape as the open alternative on the effect-level class and is answered the same way. What argues for the shift is the two poles: a written table would hold thirty-one entries of equal width and this column has two that are wider by exactly the two values a clamp absorbs at each end. That is an argument from the era and it carries the claim; it does not close it.

separated_by.why_not_separable: Two ways of arriving at one number differ in where the number comes from and in nothing that comes out. The claim does not rest on the difference: what it states is the thirty-one positions, their spacing and the clamp, and both readings give all three.

alternatives.reading: The positions are the ones measured here and the degrees printed beside them are the publisher's account rather than the part's. The byte reaches thirty-one places and moves between them where the rule says; what is not measured is that they are twelve degrees apart, or that the two ends are behind rather than in front.
alternatives.why_it_stands: Every number this run returned is a difference between two outputs. The curve it traces is consistent with the printed labels -- it is largest seven positions either side of centre and comes back to the centre's own reading at both ends, which is what a placement that travels round a listener does and what a placement that only travels left and right does not -- but consistent is not measured, and reading degrees out of it would be fitting this unit's outputs to somebody else's ears.

separated_by.observable: Where a listener hears each of the thirty-one positions.
separated_by.why_not_separable: Not by this archive, and not for want of a stage. What the question needs is a listener: an angle is a fact about where a sound arrives at two ears, and every reading here is a fact about what leaves two sockets. The nearest thing that could be done is to correlate the per-band separation this run published against a head-related set measured somewhere else, which would be a fit of this unit to another measurement rather than a measurement of this unit, and belongs to whoever has both.

compared_against.generated_from: The rule as published, with no number in it fitted here or anywhere: the centre, the step and the stop are read off the page's own labels. It is evaluated at every byte value and turned into the one thing a reading between two channels can check -- which pairs of neighbouring settings must differ and which must not.
compared_against.why_not_a_filter: There is nothing to filter. The set is one record, and it is every reading this byte has: the whole sweep, at every value the byte takes.

the_margin.why_this_is_the_denominator: Not the run's take-to-take floor, which is smaller. What a step across a boundary has to clear is the largest distance any two settings the rule calls one place came back apart -- because that is what this reading says one place is worth, measured rather than assumed, over 97 such pairs.

the_five_that_moved_inside_a_position.why_they_are_not_a_breakdown: Each is within half a decibel of a tenth of the smallest step the rule says is a boundary, and they sit in five different positions rather than in one. A wider table would put them all at the same distance from each other and a byte read straight would move at every step; what these do is sit at the floor.

the_two_poles.read_as: The rule says the two ends of the byte are one place, and they came back 0.006 decibels apart against a floor of 0.03. They also came back at the centre's own reading, which is what a placement directly behind a listener does to two outputs and is not something the rule predicted -- it is reported and not claimed.

the_other_type_carrying_this_byte.what: Read after the movement stops, the second type carrying this byte returns the same thirty-one placements -- one setting inside each position, in both output modes.

against_the_published_positions.what: The same reading held against `by_position_db` above, which was taken from the other type.

the_other_type_carrying_this_byte.why_this_is_not_another_test_of_the_rule: A grid landing one setting inside each position samples a table and a law at the same places, which is what this claim already says of every coarse run. What it tests is that the two types the byte is printed against return the same thirty-one readings, which had not been measured: the earlier sweep of this type read its movement.
the_other_type_carrying_this_byte.what_the_reading_is_worth: Thirty-one readings in each of two output modes against a run whose steadiest setting repeats to a hundredth of a decibel. Nothing was fitted to this type, so all sixty-two were places it could have disagreed.

what_the_first_reading_of_the_other_type.what: This claim rested on two verdicts of the earlier 01 70 sweep, one of them `did_not_repeat_within_a_setting: true`, read as a reading of the byte. It is a reading of the movement: that type reaches the placement its byte names over seconds and the sweep took its takes without waiting.
what_the_first_reading_of_the_other_type.why_it_is_named_rather_than_dropped: It was rested on. A claim that quietly stops resting on something is a claim whose history cannot be read, and the record itself is not retracted -- it is what takes struck without waiting return.
what_the_first_reading_of_the_other_type.how_far_it_was_out: Up to 20.56 dB in Phones and 10.30 in Speaker against the same settings read after arrival.
what_the_first_reading_of_the_other_type.and_the_verdict_it_carried: The same movement returned `true` in Phones and `false` in Speaker -- the widest setting spreads 13.34 dB in one and 9.80 in the other, either side of a bar at twelve. The bar is not moved to suit them: a threshold changed to fit a result is the one repair this archive does not make, and what was wrong here is the reading and not the bar.

the_table_is_a_mirror.what: Every position and the one opposite it put the same distance between the two outputs, with the sign turned round. So what a part rendering this needs is 16 numbers and a sign rather than 31 numbers.
the_table_is_a_mirror.how_it_was_read: The chain has an imbalance of its own, and this reading measures it rather than correcting for it: the centre and the two ends are the three places the table itself puts in the middle between the outputs, and they came back within a few hundredths of each other. Their mean is what is taken off before the two sides are added together.
the_table_is_a_mirror.against: the widest distance any two settings the rule calls one place came back apart, which this run measured at 0.045 dB
the_table_is_a_mirror.why_it_is_not_a_test_of_the_rule: The rule names which position a byte is in and says nothing about what a position does to the output. A table of thirty-one free entries would satisfy it and could still be lopsided, so the mirror is a second thing the readings say and not a second place the rule could have been wrong.

a_sweep_beside_the_one_that_closed_it.why_they_are_not_another_test_of_the_rul: Each asks one setting inside each position, and a grid like that returns the same numbers from a table of thirty-one entries as from the rule that generates them. What tests the rule is the whole byte, which is the sweep this claim already rests on.

what_the_other_output_mode_says.read_as: The centre and the two ends are where the placement is in the middle between the outputs however it is rendered, and the two modes return them to within a few hundredths of a decibel of each other. Between those places the two modes part company by many decibels, which is the cancellation one of them has to do and the other does not -- so this is evidence that both modes read one table and none at all about what the table holds.

what_the_turning_type_says.read_as: Nothing yet. `01 70` is the same parameter on the type that turns, and its takes do not repeat inside a setting: two takes of one azimuth came back up to 13.34 decibels apart where the same reading on the still type repeated to a hundredth. The turn byte was written to the state the page prints as Off and the speed byte to the bottom of its printed range, and the placement moved anyway -- which is a fact about that type and not about this byte. So the claim covers `01 70` on the page's word alone, and what would settle it is finding what stops that type rather than another sweep of this one.
